failures.summary: Empirically demonstrated: on a COMPLETE file ending in a trailing newline the reader returns a blank line at offset = last-content-line + 1 with no warning. The diff-added gloss 'a blank line is content, since the file continues past it' is false in that case — the file does not continue past it.

PARTIALLY UPHELD on orchestrator re-check. The verifier is right that a preflight-guaranteed file-side length channel exists: `git cat-file -s $(git hash-object skills/review/SKILL.md)` returns 57775, matching `wc -c`, using only git (preflight guarantees are git gh jq python3 PyYAML). So 'none is guaranteed installed' is imprecise as written. But the verifier's conclusion overreaches: the missing half is the READER-side comparand — the agent cannot measure how many bytes its own reader delivered — so no comparison is actually available, and the operative rule (do not substitute an external count for the confirming read) is sound. A line-count comparison would work on the local tier via python3 but not on the cloud tier, where the interpreter head is denied, so the absolute 'nothing on this path distinguishes' is over-strong for one tier. Graded Suggestion; does not change the verdict.

The changeset claims the Step 1 dispatch paragraph and shadow-review.md's subagent arm BOTH require carrying resolution steps 3 and 4 verbatim. shadow-review.md requires only 'Step 1's completeness predicate — carried into that subagent's prompt by the parent'; it names neither step 4 nor 'verbatim'.

phase3_findings.description: The degraded engine-read arm fetches the completeness predicate with no completeness check of its own — policy without mechanism. It routes on 'if that predicate read does not succeed', which is the same 'a body came back' test this PR exists to replace. Measured: skills/review-and-fix/references/loop-control.md is 60,211 bytes (97.5% of the 61,750-byte lint ceiling) and the predicate occupies bytes 39,005-45,837 (65-76% through the file), so a truncation anywhere in lines 166-194 delivers a body that reads as a complete Step 1 and contains no predicate. The same paragraph removes the agent's other source of that mechanism ('review-and-fix did not load on this arm'). Fails OPEN on a merge gate: the run proceeds to inline engine execution with no predicate, accepts a fragmentary engine root, and stamps the PR review-ready. Remedy is cheap — unlike the engine root, loop-control.md carries a boundary pair ('# Reference: Loop Control …' / '<!-- END loop-control.md -->'), so the arm can require that pair rather than an end-of-file confirmation.

The changeset bullet is false against HEAD on both limbs. Limb 1: it claims the Step 1 dispatch paragraph and shadow-review.md's subagent arm 'both require the parent to carry resolution steps 3 and 4 into the subagent's prompt verbatim'. loop-control.md line 165 does; shadow-review.md line 39 requires only 'Step 1's completeness predicate — carried into that subagent's prompt by the parent' — neither naming step 4 nor requiring verbatim. This is substantive: step 4's Engine-subagent arm declares itself binding on 'the Step 1 or Step 2.6 dispatch' and is what tells that subagent to return the engine-root: incomplete terminal in place of a fanned-out payload, yet the shadow site does not require that arm to reach the fresh context it says holds none of Step 1. Limb 2: 'leaving the predicate itself stated in exactly one place' is contradicted by the same diff adding a full restatement to docs/internal/DEVFLOW_SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md — mitigated but not made true by that restatement self-labelling non-authoritative.

Intra-diff contradiction on the same symbol (iter-<N>.json). Diff-ADDED at loop-control.md line 191: 'The halt never reaches Step 3, so this iteration's fused iter-<N>.json emit never fires.' RETAINED and unreconciled at skills/implement/phases/phase-3-fix-loop.md line 37: 'the per-iteration effectiveness record (iter-<N>.json) is a non-optional emit on every iteration … and the emit is non-optional on every path, including a degraded one' — the paragraph immediately preceding the line this diff modified. Also retained at skills/review-and-fix/SKILL.md line 298: 'mandatory on every iteration regardless of how the loop was executed — … hand-run via direct Agent dispatch on a degraded path'. An orchestrator on the degraded arm reads two shipped instructions in conflict, and the cheap wrong resolution is to fabricate an iter-1.json for an iteration that produced no review, polluting the effectiveness telemetry the emit exists to make trustworthy. Both retained sites needed a one-clause carve-out in this change.

Diff-added deictic is false against HEAD: loop-control.md line 191 says 'the blocked record below … stands in as that iteration's record', but loop-control.md contains no blocked record and no further occurrence of 'blocked' after line 191 — the record lives in the caller's file, which the very next sentence correctly identifies. Read literally it sends an agent scanning this file for a sink it will not find. Fail direction is benign; the fix is 'the caller's own blocked record'.

The justification clause attached to the blank-line rule is false for the end-of-file case. Probed directly: a complete 3-line file ending in a trailing newline returns a blank numbered line at offset 4 with no warning; the same shape appears on skills/review/SKILL.md at offset 341. The rule itself ('a blank line is content') is correct and necessary — a truncated body's next undelivered line may well be blank — and the procedure still terminates in one extra read, which this run demonstrated. But 'since the file continues past it' is demonstrably false at EOF, and the real, undocumented consequence is that EVERY intact read now costs one extra confirming read on a trailing-newline file. Reword the gloss and state the cost.

The overview's restatement presents the terminal's disposition as a two-way split (Step 1 entry / Step 2.6 shadow entry), silently dropping the third arm — Engine-subagent entry — which is the one the loop reaches FIRST on every entry, since both entries dispatch before any inline read. A maintainer reading only the overview would conclude the subagent path is ungated, the exact gap a prior iteration closed. CAPPED at Suggestion by the Phase 4.1.5 behavior-inert prose cap: both limbs hold — no tool parses it for behavior, and docs/internal/ is pruned by vendor-slice.sh so it reaches no consumer.

Step 3 requires an unestablished-resolution advance to be recorded, 'naming in this run's report which candidate it advanced past and why', and states that an unrecorded advance 'hides a present-but-unreadable engine behind a later copy'. But the Step 1 return-file field set is closed and carries no advanced-past-candidate slot, so on a fanned-out engine-subagent return the record dies with the subagent's context. Reachable via the subagent's free-text return, which is why this is a Suggestion rather than higher.

Two absolutes in the diff-added line are over-strong. 'Do not substitute a byte or line count from an external counting tool, whose absence yields an empty value and the wrong outcome' — accurate about wc/cut, but a preflight-guaranteed file-side length channel does exist: git cat-file -s $(git hash-object <file>) returns the exact byte size using only git, which lib/preflight.sh guarantees. And 'nothing on this path distinguishes an intact engine on a reader that cannot page from a truncated one' holds on the cloud tier (the python3 interpreter head is denied there) but is over-strong on the local tier, where a python3 line count is available. The operative RULE is sound — the genuinely missing half is the reader-side comparand, since the agent cannot measure how many bytes its own reader delivered — so the fix is to scope the two absolutes, not to weaken the predicate.

Headroom advisory, not a defect: loop-control.md grew 53,381 -> 60,211 bytes (1,539 under the 61,750 ceiling) and shadow-review.md grew 60,871 -> 61,180 (570 under). lint-reference-size.py is green today, but the next ordinary prose addition to either turns the required check RED. Some growth is avoidable under CLAUDE.md's instruction-plus-one-consequence rule — step 3's new paragraphs carry several rationale clauses per instruction.

other_new_important.description: The engine subagent's completeness check is unobservable to the parent — the return contract has no attestation operand. The parent must carry steps 3 and 4 verbatim, and the well-formedness check validates phase3_dispatched, expected_reviewers, verdict, diff_profile and cap_drops field by field, but completeness is the one guarantee with NO returned field. A subagent that never received the predicate (a truncated parent prompt, or a pre-#1603 vendored loop-control.md under autoUpdate:true) returns a fully well-formed fanned-out payload over a fragment and every parent check passes. Remedy costs one field plus one not-well-formed trigger.

An unclassifiable resolution advances the scan and can substitute a DIFFERENT engine copy, and on the fanned-out dispatch path the mandated 'record of the advance' has no channel — the return file's enumerated fields carry no slot for a skipped candidate. This also weakens the self-review skew guard by exactly its worth: the diff now concedes a self-review resolves the branch's own engine 'unless that candidate's own resolution is left unestablished, which advances the scan to a vendored copy', three lines from the still-standing 'do not silently fall back to a stale plugin-cache copy'. Shadow suggests refusing the advance when the diff is engine_self_modifying.
